NASB.1: Then it happened when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, that the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev and on Ziklag, and had overthrown Ziklag and burned it with fire;
NASB.2: and they took captive the women [and all] who were in it, both small and great, without killing anyone, and carried [them] off and went their way.
NASB.3: When David and his men came to the city, behold, it was burned with fire, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
NASB.4: Then David and the people who were with him lifted their voices and wept until there was no strength in them to weep.
NASB.5: Now David's two wives had been taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite.
NASB.6: Moreover David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, for all the people were embittered, each one because of his sons and his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
NASB.7: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, 'Please bring me the ephod.' So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
NASB.8: David inquired of the LORD, saying, 'Shall I pursue this band? Shall I overtake them?' And He said to him, 'Pursue, for you will surely overtake them, and you will surely rescue [all].'
NASB.9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and came to the brook Besor, [where] those left behind remained.
NASB.10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men, for two hundred who were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor remained [behind].
NASB.11: Now they found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David, and gave him bread and he ate, and they provided him water to drink.
NASB.12: They gave him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins, and he ate; then his spirit revived. For he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
NASB.13: David said to him, 'To whom do you belong? And where are you from?' And he said, 'I am a young man of Egypt, a servant of an Amalekite; and my master left me behind when I fell sick three days ago.
NASB.14: 'We made a raid on the Negev of the Cherethites, and on that which belongs to Judah, and on the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.'
NASB.15: Then David said to him, 'Will you bring me down to this band?' And he said, 'Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down to this band.'
NASB.16: When he had brought him down, behold, they were spread over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing because of all the great spoil that they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
NASB.17: David slaughtered them from the twilight until the evening of the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.
NASB.18: So David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and rescued his two wives.
NASB.19: But nothing of theirs was missing, whether small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything that they had taken for themselves; David brought [it] all back.
NASB.20: So David had captured all the sheep and the cattle [which the people] drove ahead of the [other] livestock, and they said, 'This is David's spoil.'
NASB.21: When David came to the two hundred men who were too exhausted to follow David, who had also been left at the brook Besor, and they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him, then David approached the people and greeted them.
NASB.22: Then all the wicked and worthless men among those who went with David said, 'Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his children, that they may lead [them] away and depart.'
NASB.23: Then David said, 'You must not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us, who has kept us and delivered into our hand the band that came against us.
NASB.24: 'And who will listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down to the battle, so shall his share be who stays by the baggage; they shall share alike.'
NASB.25: So it has been from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
NASB.26: Now when David came to Ziklag, he sent [some] of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, 'Behold, a gift for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD:
NASB.27: to those who were in Bethel, and to those who were in Ramoth of the Negev, and to those who were in Jattir,
NASB.28: and to those who were in Aroer, and to those who were in Siphmoth, and to those who were in Eshtemoa,
NASB.29: and to those who were in Racal, and to those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and to those who were in the cities of the Kenites,
NASB.30: and to those who were in Hormah, and to those who were in Bor-ashan, and to those who were in Athach,
NASB.31: and to those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were accustomed to go.'

NKJV.1: Now it happened, when David and his men came to Ziklag, on the third day, that the Amalekites had invaded the South and Ziklag, attacked Ziklag and burned it with fire,
NKJV.2: and had taken captive the women and those who were there, from small to great; they did not kill anyone, but carried them away and went their way.
NKJV.3: So David and his men came to the city, and there it was, burned with fire; and their wives, their sons, and their daughters had been taken captive.
NKJV.4: Then David and the people who were with him lifted up their voices and wept, until they had no more power to weep.
NKJV.5: And David’s two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite, had been taken captive.
NKJV.6: Now David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
NKJV.7: Then David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, “Please bring the ephod here to me.” And Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
NKJV.8: So David inquired of the LORD, saying, “Shall I pursue this troop? Shall I overtake them?” And He answered him, “Pursue, for you shall surely overtake them and without fail recover all.”
NKJV.9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and came to the Brook Besor, where those stayed who were left behind.
NKJV.10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for two hundred stayed behind, who were so weary that they could not cross the Brook Besor.
NKJV.11: Then they found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David; and they gave him bread and he ate, and they let him drink water.
NKJV.12: And they gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. So when he had eaten, his strength came back to him; for he had eaten no bread nor drunk water for three days and three nights.
NKJV.13: Then David said to him, “To whom do you belong, and where are you from?” And he said, “I am a young man from Egypt, servant of an Amalekite; and my master left me behind, because three days ago I fell sick.
NKJV.14: We made an invasion of the southern area of the Cherethites, in the territory which belongs to Judah, and of the southern area of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.”
NKJV.15: And David said to him, “Can you take me down to this troop?” So he said, “Swear to me by God that you will neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will take you down to this troop.”
NKJV.16: And when he had brought him down, there they were, spread out over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil which they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
NKJV.17: Then David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode on camels and fled.
NKJV.18: So David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, and David rescued his two wives.
NKJV.19: And nothing of theirs was lacking, either small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything which they had taken from them; David recovered all.
NKJV.20: Then David took all the flocks and herds they had driven before those other livestock, and said, “This is David’s spoil.”
NKJV.21: Now David came to the two hundred men who had been so weary that they could not follow David, whom they also had made to stay at the Brook Besor. So they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And when David came near the people, he greeted them.
NKJV.22: Then all the wicked and worthless men of those who went with David answered and said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except for every man’s wife and children, that they may lead them away and depart.”
NKJV.23: But David said, “My brethren, you shall not do so with what the LORD has given us, who has preserved us and delivered into our hand the troop that came against us.
NKJV.24: For who will heed you in this matter? But as his part is who goes down to the battle, so shall his part be who stays by the supplies; they shall share alike.”
NKJV.25: So it was, from that day forward; he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
NKJV.26: Now when David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the spoil to the elders of Judah, to his friends, saying, “Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD”—
NKJV.27: to those who were in Bethel, those who were in Ramoth of the South, those who were in Jattir,
NKJV.28: those who were in Aroer, those who were in Siphmoth, those who were in Eshtemoa,
NKJV.29: those who were in Rachal, those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, those who were in the cities of the Kenites,
NKJV.30: those who were in Hormah, those who were in Chorashan, those who were in Athach,
NKJV.31: those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were accustomed to rove.

ESV.1: Now when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid against the Negeb and against Ziklag. They had overcome Ziklag and burned it with fire
ESV.2: and taken captive the women and all  who were in it, both small and great. They killed no one, but carried them off and went their way.
ESV.3: And when David and his men came to the city, they found it burned with fire, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.
ESV.4: Then David and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept until they had no more strength to weep.
ESV.5: David's two wives also had been taken captive, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
ESV.6: And David was greatly distressed, for the people spoke of stoning him, because all the people were bitter in soul,  each for his sons and daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
ESV.7: And David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
ESV.8: And David inquired of the LORD, “Shall I pursue after this band? Shall I overtake them?” He answered him, “Pursue, for you shall surely overtake and shall surely rescue.”
ESV.9: So David set out, and the six hundred men who were with him, and they came to the brook Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.
ESV.10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men. Two hundred stayed behind, who were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor.
ESV.11: They found an Egyptian in the open country and brought him to David. And they gave him bread and he ate. They gave him water to drink,
ESV.12: and they gave him a piece of a cake of figs and two clusters of raisins. And when he had eaten, his spirit revived, for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
ESV.13: And David said to him, “To whom do you belong? And where are you from?” He said, “I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite, and my master left me behind because I fell sick three days ago.
ESV.14: We had made a raid against the Negeb of the Cherethites and against that which belongs to Judah and against the Negeb of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire.”
ESV.15: And David said to him, “Will you take me down to this band?” And he said, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will take you down to this band.”
ESV.16: And when he had taken him down, behold, they were spread abroad over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing, because of all the great spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
ESV.17: And David struck them down from twilight until the evening of the next day, and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men, who mounted camels and fled.
ESV.18: David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and David rescued his two wives.
ESV.19: Nothing was missing, whether small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything that had been taken. David brought back all.
ESV.20: David also captured all the flocks and herds, and the people drove the livestock before him,  and said, “This is David's spoil.”
ESV.21: Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David, and who had been left at the brook Besor. And they went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. And when David came near to the people he greeted them.
ESV.22: Then all the wicked and worthless fellows among the men who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except that each man may lead away his wife and children, and depart.”
ESV.23: But David said, “You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He has preserved us and given into our hand the band that came against us.
ESV.24: Who would listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down into the battle, so shall his share be who stays by the baggage. They shall share alike.”
ESV.25: And he made it a statute and a rule for Israel from that day forward to this day.
ESV.26: When David came to Ziklag, he sent part of the spoil to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD.”
ESV.27: It was for those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negeb, in Jattir,
ESV.28: in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa,
ESV.29: in Racal, in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, in the cities of the Kenites,
ESV.30: in Hormah, in Bor-ashan, in Athach,
ESV.31: in Hebron, for all the places where David and his men had roamed.

WEB.1: When David and his men had come to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid on the South, and on Ziklag, and had struck Ziklag, and burned it with fire,
WEB.2: and had taken captive the women and all who were in it, both small and great. They didn’t kill any, but carried them off, and went their way.
WEB.3: When David and his men came to the city, behold, it was burned with fire; and their wives, their sons, and their daughters were taken captive.
WEB.4: Then David and the people who were with him lifted up their voice and wept until they had no more power to weep.
WEB.5: David’s two wives were taken captive, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
WEB.6: David was greatly distressed; for the people spoke of stoning him, because the souls of all the people were grieved, every man for his sons and for his daughters; but David strengthened himself in Yahweh his God.
WEB.7: David said to Abiathar the priest, the son of Ahimelech, “Please bring the ephod here to me.” Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
WEB.8: David inquired of Yahweh, saying, “If I pursue after this troop, will I overtake them?” He answered him, “Pursue; for you will surely overtake them, and will without fail recover all.”
WEB.9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those who were left behind stayed.
WEB.10: But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for two hundred stayed behind, who were so faint that they couldn’t go over the brook Besor.
WEB.11: They found an Egyptian in the field, and brought him to David, and gave him bread, and he ate; and they gave him water to drink.
WEB.12: They gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his spirit came again to him; for he had eaten no bread, and drank no water for three days and three nights.
WEB.13: David asked him, “To whom do you belong? Where are you from?” He said, “I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite; and my master left me, because three days ago I got sick.
WEB.14: We made a raid on the South of the Cherethites, and on that which belongs to Judah, and on the South of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag with fire.”
WEB.15: David said to him, “Will you bring me down to this troop?” He said, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me and not deliver me up into the hands of my master, and I will bring you down to this troop.”
WEB.16: When he had brought him down, behold, they were spread around over all the ground, eating, drinking, and dancing, because of all the great plunder that they had taken out of the land of the Philistines, and out of the land of Judah.
WEB.17: David struck them from the twilight even to the evening of the next day. Not a man of them escaped from there, except four hundred young men, who rode on camels and fled.
WEB.18: David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken; and David rescued his two wives.
WEB.19: There was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither plunder, nor anything that they had taken to them. David brought back all.
WEB.20: David took all the flocks and the herds, which they drove before those other livestock, and said, “This is David’s plunder.”
WEB.21: David came to the two hundred men, who were so faint that they could not follow David, whom also they had made to stay at the brook Besor; and they went out to meet David, and to meet the people who were with him. When David came near to the people, he greeted them.
WEB.22: Then all the wicked men and base fellows, of those who went with David, answered and said, “Because they didn’t go with us, we will not give them anything of the plunder that we have recovered, except to every man his wife and his children, that he may lead them away, and depart.”
WEB.23: Then David said, “Do not do so, my brothers, with that which Yahweh has given to us, who has preserved us, and delivered the troop that came against us into our hand.
WEB.24: Who will listen to you in this matter? For as his share is who goes down to the battle, so shall his share be who stays with the baggage. They shall share alike.”
WEB.25: It was so from that day forward, that he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
WEB.26: When David came to Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder to the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, “Behold, a present for you from the plunder of Yahweh’s enemies.”
WEB.27: He sent it to those who were in Bethel, to those who were in Ramoth of the South, to those who were in Jattir,
WEB.28: to those who were in Aroer, to those who were in Siphmoth, to those who were in Eshtemoa,
WEB.29: to those who were in Racal, to those who were in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, to those who were in the cities of the Kenites,
WEB.30: to those who were in Hormah, to those who were in Borashan, to those who were in Athach,
WEB.31: to those who were in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men used to stay.

AMP.1: Now it happened when David and his men came [home] to Ziklag on the third day, [they found] that the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negev (the South country) and on Ziklag, and had overthrown Ziklag and burned it with fire;

AMP.3: When David and his men came to the town, it was burned, and their wives and their sons and their daughters had been taken captive.
AMP.4: Then David and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept until they were too exhausted to weep [any longer].
AMP.5: Now David's two wives had been captured, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the widow of Nabal the Carmelite.
AMP.6: Further, David was greatly distressed because the people spoke of stoning him, for all of them were embittered, each man for his sons and daughters. But David felt strengthened and encouraged in the LORD his God.
AMP.7: David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, "Please bring me the ephod." So Abiathar brought him the ephod.
AMP.8: David inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I pursue this band [of raiders]? Will I overtake them?" And He answered him, "Pursue, for you will certainly overtake them, and you will certainly rescue [the captives]."
AMP.9: So David went, he and the six hundred men who were with him, and came to the brook Besor; there those [who could not continue] remained behind.
AMP.10: But David pursued [the Amalekites], he and four hundred men, for two hundred who were too exhausted to cross the brook Besor stayed behind.
AMP.11: They found an Egyptian [who had collapsed] in the field and brought him to David, and gave him bread and he ate, and they gave him water to drink,
AMP.12: and they gave him a piece of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins; and when he had eaten, his energy returned, for he had not eaten bread or had any water to drink for three days and three nights.
AMP.13: David said to him, "To whom do you belong, and where are you from?" He said, "I am a young man from Egypt, a servant of an Amalekite; and my master abandoned me [as useless] when I fell sick three days ago.
AMP.14: We made a raid on the Negev of the Cherethites, and on that which belongs to Judah, and on the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag with fire."
AMP.15: Then David said to him, "Will you take me down to this band [of raiders]?" And he said, "Swear to me by God that you will not kill me or turn me over to the hand of my master, and I will bring you down to this band."
AMP.16: When he brought David down, the Amalekites had disbanded and spread over all the land, eating and drinking and dancing because of all the great spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
AMP.17: Then David [and his men] struck them down [in battle] from twilight until the evening of the next day; and not a man of them escaped, except four hundred young men who rode camels and fled.
AMP.18: So David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken, and rescued his two wives.
AMP.19: Nothing of theirs was missing whether small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything that had been taken; David recovered it all.
AMP.20: So David captured all the flocks and herds [which the enemy had], and [the people] drove those animals before him and said, "This is David's spoil."
AMP.21: David came to the two hundred men who were so exhausted that they could not follow him and had been left at the brook Besor [with the provisions]. They went out to meet David and the people with him, and when he approached the people, he greeted them.
AMP.22: Then all the wicked and worthless men among those who went with David said, "Because they did not go with us, we will give them none of the spoil that we have recovered, except that each man may take his wife and children away and leave."
AMP.23: David said, "You must not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us safe and has handed over to us the band [of Amalekites] that came against us.
AMP.24: And who will listen to you in regard to this matter? For as is the share of him who goes down into the battle, so shall his share be who stays by the provisions and supplies; they shall share alike."
AMP.25: So from that day forward he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel to this day.
AMP.26: When David came to Ziklag, he sent part of the spoil to the elders of Judah, his friends, saying, "Here is a blessing (gift) for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD:
AMP.27: For those in Bethel, Ramoth of the Negev, Jattir,

NLT.1: Three days later, when David and his men arrived home at their town of Ziklag, they found that the Amalekites had made a raid into the Negev and Ziklag; they had crushed Ziklag and burned it to the ground.
NLT.2: They had carried off the women and children and everyone else but without killing anyone.
NLT.3: When David and his men saw the ruins and realized what had happened to their families,
NLT.4: they wept until they could weep no more.
NLT.5: David’s two wives, Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel, were among those captured.
NLT.6: David was now in great danger because all his men were very bitter about losing their sons and daughters, and they began to talk of stoning him. But David found strength in the LORD his God.
NLT.7: Then he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring me the ephod!” So Abiathar brought it.
NLT.8: Then David asked the LORD, “Should I chase after this band of raiders? Will I catch them?” And the LORD told him, “Yes, go after them. You will surely recover everything that was taken from you!”
NLT.9: So David and his 600 men set out, and they came to the brook Besor.
NLT.10: But 200 of the men were too exhausted to cross the brook, so David continued the pursuit with 400 men.
NLT.11: Along the way they found an Egyptian man in a field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread to eat and water to drink.
NLT.12: They also gave him part of a fig cake and two clusters of raisins, for he hadn’t had anything to eat or drink for three days and nights. Before long his strength returned.
NLT.13: “To whom do you belong, and where do you come from?” David asked him. “I am an Egyptian — the slave of an Amalekite,” he replied. “My master abandoned me three days ago because I was sick.
NLT.14: We were on our way back from raiding the Kerethites in the Negev, the territory of Judah, and the land of Caleb, and we had just burned Ziklag.”
NLT.15: “Will you lead me to this band of raiders?” David asked. The young man replied, “If you take an oath in God’s name that you will not kill me or give me back to my master, then I will guide you to them.”
NLT.16: So he led David to them, and they found the Amalekites spread out across the fields, eating and drinking and dancing with joy because of the vast amount of plunder they had taken from the Philistines and the land of Judah.
NLT.17: David and his men rushed in among them and slaughtered them throughout that night and the entire next day until evening. None of the Amalekites escaped except 400 young men who fled on camels.

NLT.19: Nothing was missing: small or great, son or daughter, nor anything else that had been taken. David brought everything back.

NLT.21: Then David returned to the brook Besor and met up with the 200 men who had been left behind because they were too exhausted to go with him. They went out to meet David and his men, and David greeted them joyfully.
NLT.22: But some evil troublemakers among David’s men said, “They didn’t go with us, so they can’t have any of the plunder we recovered. Give them their wives and children, and tell them to be gone.”
NLT.23: But David said, “No, my brothers! Don’t be selfish with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us safe and helped us defeat the band of raiders that attacked us.
NLT.24: Who will listen when you talk like this? We share and share alike — those who go to battle and those who guard the equipment.”
NLT.25: From then on David made this a decree and regulation for Israel, and it is still followed today.
NLT.26: When he arrived at Ziklag, David sent part of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends. “Here is a present for you, taken from the LORD’s enemies,” he said.
NLT.27: The gifts were sent to the people of the following towns David had visited: Bethel, Ramoth-negev, Jattir,
NLT.29: Racal, the towns of the Jerahmeelites, the towns of the Kenites,
NLT.31: Hebron, and all the other places David and his men had visited.

MSG.1: Three days later, David and his men arrived back in Ziklag. Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They tore Ziklag to pieces and then burned it down.
MSG.2: They captured all the women, young and old. They didn't kill anyone, but drove them like a herd of cattle.
MSG.3: By the time David and his men entered the village, it had been burned to the ground, and their wives, sons, and daughters all taken prisoner.
MSG.4: David and his men burst out in loud wails—wept and wept until they were exhausted with weeping.
MSG.5: David's two wives, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail widow of Nabal of Carmel, had been taken prisoner along with the rest.
MSG.6:
And suddenly David was in even worse trouble. There was talk among the men, bitter over the loss of their families, of stoning him.
David strengthened himself with trust in his God.
MSG.7: He ordered Abiathar the priest, son of Ahimelech, "Bring me the Ephod so I can consult God." Abiathar brought it to David.
MSG.8:
Then David prayed to God, "Shall I go after these raiders? Can I catch them?"
The answer came, "Go after them! Yes, you'll catch them! Yes, you'll make the rescue!"
MSG.9: David went, he and the six hundred men with him. They arrived at the Brook Besor, where some of them dropped out.
MSG.10: David and four hundred men kept up the pursuit, but two hundred of them were too fatigued to cross the Brook Besor, and stayed there.
MSG.11: Some who went on came across an Egyptian in a field and took him to David. They gave him bread and he ate. And he drank some water.
MSG.12: They gave him a piece of fig cake and a couple of raisin muffins. Life began to revive in him. He hadn't eaten or drunk a thing for three days and nights!
MSG.13:
David said to him, "Who do you belong to? Where are you from?"
"I'm an Egyptian slave of an Amalekite," he said. "My master walked off and left me when I got sick—that was three days ago.
MSG.14: We had raided the Negev of the Kerethites, of Judah, and of Caleb. Ziklag we burned."
MSG.15:
David asked him, "Can you take us to the raiders?"
"Promise me by God," he said, "that you won't kill me or turn me over to my old master, and I'll take you straight to the raiders."
MSG.16: He led David to them. They were scattered all over the place, eating and drinking, gorging themselves on all the loot they had plundered from Philistia and Judah.
MSG.17: David pounced. He fought them from before sunrise until evening of the next day. None got away except for four hundred of the younger men who escaped by riding off on camels.
MSG.18: David rescued everything the Amalekites had taken. And he rescued his two wives!
MSG.19: Nothing and no one was missing—young or old, son or daughter, plunder or whatever. David recovered the whole lot.
MSG.20: He herded the sheep and cattle before them, and they all shouted, "David's plunder!"
MSG.21: Then David came to the two hundred who had been too tired to continue with him and had dropped out at the Brook Besor. They came out to welcome David and his band. As he came near he called out, "Success!"
MSG.22: But all the mean-spirited men who had marched with David, the rabble element, objected: "They didn't help in the rescue, they don't get any of the plunder we recovered. Each man can have his wife and children, but that's it. Take them and go!"
MSG.23: "Families don't do this sort of thing! Oh no, my brothers!" said David as he broke up the argument. "You can't act this way with what God gave us! God kept us safe. He handed over the raiders who attacked us.
MSG.24: Who would ever listen to this kind of talk? The share of the one who stays with the gear is the share of the one who fights—equal shares. Share and share alike!"
MSG.25: From that day on, David made that the rule in Israel—and it still is.
MSG.26: On returning to Ziklag, David sent portions of the plunder to the elders of Judah, his neighbors, with a note saying, "A gift from the plunder of God's enemies!"
MSG.27: He sent them to the elders in Bethel, Ramoth Negev, Jattir,
MSG.31: and Hebron, along with a number of other places David and his men went to from time to time.

NRSVCE.1: Now when David and his men came to Ziklag on the third day, the Amalekites had made a raid on the Negeb and on Ziklag. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it down,
NRSVCE.2: and taken captive the women and all who were in it, both small and great; they killed none of them, but carried them off, and went their way.
NRSVCE.3: When David and his men came to the city, they found it burned down, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive.
NRSVCE.4: Then David and the people who were with him raised their voices and wept, until they had no more strength to weep.
NRSVCE.5: David’s two wives also had been taken captive, Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail the widow of Nabal of Carmel.
NRSVCE.6: David was in great danger; for the people spoke of stoning him, because all the people were bitter in spirit for their sons and daughters. But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.
NRSVCE.7: David said to the priest Abiathar son of Ahimelech, “Bring me the ephod.” So Abiathar brought the ephod to David.
NRSVCE.8: David inquired of the LORD, “Shall I pursue this band? Shall I overtake them?” He answered him, “Pursue; for you shall surely overtake and shall surely rescue.”
NRSVCE.9: So David set out, he and the six hundred men who were with him. They came to the Wadi Besor, where those stayed who were left behind.
NRSVCE.10: But David went on with the pursuit, he and four hundred men; two hundred stayed behind, too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor.
NRSVCE.11: In the open country they found an Egyptian, and brought him to David. They gave him bread and he ate; they gave him water to drink;
NRSVCE.12: they also gave him a piece of fig cake and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his spirit revived; for he had not eaten bread or drunk water for three days and three nights.
NRSVCE.13: Then David said to him, “To whom do you belong? Where are you from?” He said, “I am a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite. My master left me behind because I fell sick three days ago.
NRSVCE.14: We had made a raid on the Negeb of the Cherethites and on that which belongs to Judah and on the Negeb of Caleb; and we burned Ziklag down.”
NRSVCE.15: David said to him, “Will you take me down to this raiding party?” He said, “Swear to me by God that you will not kill me, or hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to them.”
NRSVCE.16: When he had taken him down, they were spread out all over the ground, eating and drinking and dancing, because of the great amount of spoil they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
NRSVCE.17: David attacked them from twilight until the evening of the next day. Not one of them escaped, except four hundred young men, who mounted camels and fled.
NRSVCE.18: David recovered all that the Amalekites had taken; and David rescued his two wives.
NRSVCE.19: Nothing was missing, whether small or great, sons or daughters, spoil or anything that had been taken; David brought back everything.
NRSVCE.20: David also captured all the flocks and herds, which were driven ahead of the other cattle; people said, “This is David’s spoil.”
NRSVCE.21: Then David came to the two hundred men who had been too exhausted to follow David, and who had been left at the Wadi Besor. They went out to meet David and to meet the people who were with him. When David drew near to the people he saluted them.
NRSVCE.22: Then all the corrupt and worthless fellows among the men who had gone with David said, “Because they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the spoil that we have recovered, except that each man may take his wife and children, and leave.”
NRSVCE.23: But David said, “You shall not do so, my brothers, with what the LORD has given us; he has preserved us and handed over to us the raiding party that attacked us.
NRSVCE.24: Who would listen to you in this matter? For the share of the one who goes down into the battle shall be the same as the share of the one who stays by the baggage; they shall share alike.”
NRSVCE.25: From that day forward he made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel; it continues to the present day.
NRSVCE.26: When David came to Ziklag, he sent part of the spoil to his friends, the elders of Judah, saying, “Here is a present for you from the spoil of the enemies of the LORD”;
NRSVCE.27: it was for those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negeb, in Jattir,
NRSVCE.28: in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa,
NRSVCE.29: in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites, in the towns of the Kenites,
NRSVCE.30: in Hormah, in Bor-ashan, in Athach,
NRSVCE.31: in Hebron, all the places where David and his men had roamed.
